```markdown
# Breaking-change flag in release notes

Source: `specs/deferred_items.md` item 7 (picked via /deferred, disposition Design).

## Intent and why
`release-notes` writes one bullet per merged pull request. Breaking changes
currently look like every other bullet. Two audiences need to spot them:
- people reading the notes, who should see breaking changes at a glance;
- `announce`, which should put breaking changes first in its post.

## Goals
- `release-notes` marks a bullet as breaking when its pull request carries the
  `breaking` label.
- `changelog-check` (`parse.py`) accepts the marked bullets and records the flag.
- `announce` lists breaking entries before all others.

## Non-goals
- No other flags or tags (no `security`, `deprecated`, etc.).
- No rewriting of release notes that already exist.
- No new way to decide what is breaking beyond the `breaking` PR label.

## Anti-goals
- Existing, untagged notes stop parsing or parse differently. That would be a
  failure even if the new tag works.

## Constraints
- `parse.py` splits each bullet on " — " and rejects a bullet with more than
  two parts. That rule stays as it is.

## Approaches
1. Append " — breaking: yes" as a third part and teach `parse.py` to accept
   three parts. Trade-off: loosens the two-part rule, so malformed bullets that
   happen to have three parts would start passing; every bullet's shape changes
   meaning.
2. Start the bullet with a `[breaking]` tag that `parse.py` reads and strips
   before it splits. Trade-off: one more thing to check at the front of each
   bullet; in return untagged bullets parse exactly as before and the tag is
   visible to readers at the start of the line.

Picked: **2**, by the partner, on my recommendation, because older notes stay
valid unchanged and the tag is readable at a glance.

## Design (as agreed)
- `release-notes`: when the PR has the `breaking` label, the bullet text starts
  with `[breaking] `.
- `parse.py`: if the bullet text starts with `[breaking]`, strip it (and the
  following space), set `breaking=True` on the entry; otherwise
  `breaking=False`. Then split on " — " with the existing two-part rule.
- `announce`: lists breaking entries first, then the rest, each group in its
  existing order.
- Tests in `skills/changelog-check/`: one tagged bullet, one untagged bullet;
  both parse, with the right `breaking` value and the same remaining fields.

## My calls (not discussed; partner may correct)
- Tag goes after the list marker: `- [breaking] Title — #123`.
- The tag is matched exactly and case-sensitively (`[breaking]`), only at the
  start of the bullet text. A `[breaking]` elsewhere is ordinary text.
- `announce` keeps breaking entries in the same relative order they had in the
  notes; no new heading unless the builder finds `announce` already groups by
  heading.

## Left to the builder
- Where in `release-notes` the PR labels are read and how the tag is added.
- The exact field name on the parsed entry if `parse.py` already has a naming
  convention (default `breaking`).
- How `announce` reorders, following its existing structure.
```
